title: Maximum Units on a Truck
hints: every box takes exactly one slot regardless of its type, so which boxes give you the most units per slot used?
sort the box types by unitsPerBox in descending order
walk the sorted list, taking as many boxes as you can from each type (min of boxes available and remaining truck capacity) before moving to the next

why can't saving room for a later, lower-value box type ever beat taking the highest-value boxes first? because slots are interchangeable and each slot's contribution is maximized independently by picking the highest unitsPerBox available
commonMistakes: sorting by numberOfBoxes instead of unitsPerBox, which loads many low-value boxes instead of few high-value ones
forgetting to cap the boxes taken from a type by both the remaining truck capacity and the boxes actually available
not stopping early once truck capacity is exhausted, wasting iteration but more importantly risking an off-by-one overfill

content.problemStatement:
You're loading a truck with total capacity `truckSize` boxes. You're
given `boxTypes`, where `boxTypes[i] = [numberOfBoxesI, unitsPerBoxI]`
describes a group of identical boxes, each holding `unitsPerBoxI` units,
and you choose which boxes to load, up to `truckSize` boxes total.

**Return the maximum total number of units you can load onto the truck.**
constraints: each boxTypes entry is [numberOfBoxes, unitsPerBox], both positive
you may load fewer than truckSize boxes if fewer boxes exist
notes: truckSize exceeds the total number of boxes available (load everything)
all box types have the same units per box

sampleTestCases.explanation: load the 1 box worth 3 units, then both boxes worth 2 units each: 3 + 2 + 2 = 7, then 1 more box worth 1 unit: 3+2+2+1=8, filling all 4 slots
load all 5 boxes worth 10 units (50), all 3 boxes worth 9 units (27), then 2 of the 4 boxes worth 7 units (14): 50+27+14=91
